subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: After the Code Mode exec-policy normalization is fixed, should OpenClaw accept policy-active Codex unified-exec routing and fresh-thread refresh as the intended security-boundary tradeoff before the Codex runtime prerequisite is packaged and proven?
rationale: The remaining choice changes tool-execution routing and session continuity for policy-active Codex users, and source review cannot decide whether maintainers want to accept that compatibility cost or wait for a stronger Codex runtime/package gate.

options.title: Fix payload normalization, then sponsor the narrow path
options.body: Normalize `code_mode_exec`, keep the PR draft until runtime proof and compatibility review are explicit, then consider this narrow positive-delivery approach.

options.title: Pause behind packaged Codex proof
options.body: Keep the draft open but blocked until OpenClaw pins or proves a Codex package that emits the required Code Mode PreToolUse event without a local patch.

options.title: Prefer a different canonical PR
options.body: Move the cluster toward the fail-closed or broader enforcement PR if maintainers decide positive native delivery is not ready to own.

recommendation.title: Fix payload normalization, then sponsor the narrow path
recommendation.body: Normalize `code_mode_exec`, keep the PR draft until runtime proof and compatibility review are explicit, then consider this narrow positive-delivery approach.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent source history ties Peter Steinberger to the same native hook relay and Code Mode hook metadata surfaces, and the remaining decision is a security/compatibility boundary choice in that area.
